name: Captopril
summary: First class of drugs shown to reduce mortality and morbidity and improve symptoms in HFrEF; recommended in all patients with HFrEF unless contraindicated or not tolerated, uptitrated to the highest recommended dose (intermediate doses if target not tolerated).
points: Target dose derived from post-MI trials
cautions: Give with caution if SBP <100 mmHg, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m², or K⁺ >5.2 mEq/L
Avoid abrupt withdrawal (clinical deterioration); if ARNI is not possible, continued ACE-I remains strongly advised
Wash-out of at least 36 h before starting an ARNI (angio-oedema risk)

name: Enalapril
summary: First class of drugs shown to reduce mortality and morbidity and improve symptoms in HFrEF; recommended in all patients with HFrEF unless contraindicated or not tolerated, uptitrated to the highest recommended dose (intermediate doses if target not tolerated).
points: Comparator in PARADIGM-HF (ARNI reduced CV death/HFH by 20% vs enalapril)
cautions: Give with caution if SBP <100 mmHg, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m², or K⁺ >5.2 mEq/L

points: Higher dose reduces morbidity/mortality vs lower dose, but no substantive placebo-controlled trial; optimal dose uncertain

Avoid abrupt withdrawal (clinical deterioration); if ARNI is not possible, continued ACE-I remains strongly advised

name: Trandolapril
summary: First class of drugs shown to reduce mortality and morbidity and improve symptoms in HFrEF; recommended in all patients with HFrEF unless contraindicated or not tolerated, uptitrated to the highest recommended dose (intermediate doses if target not tolerated).
points: Target dose derived from post-MI trials
PEACE subgroup: mortality reduction in LVEF 40–50%
cautions: Give with caution if SBP <100 mmHg, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m², or K⁺ >5.2 mEq/L
Avoid abrupt withdrawal (clinical deterioration); if ARNI is not possible, continued ACE-I remains strongly advised
Wash-out of at least 36 h before starting an ARNI (angio-oedema risk)

name: Sacubitril–valsartan (ARNI)
summary: Angiotensin receptor–neprilysin inhibitor. In PARADIGM-HF it reduced CV death or HFH by 20% vs enalapril, with better QoL, slower eGFR decline, lower loop-diuretic dose and lower hyperkalaemia risk. Patients tolerating an ACE-I/ARB with persistent symptoms should be switched; may also be used de novo.
points: Optional lower start 24/26 mg b.i.d. for history of symptomatic hypotension, ACE-I-naïve patients, or eGFR 30–60 mL/min/1.73 m²
HFpEF: PARAGON-HF missed its primary endpoint; benefit seen with LVEF below ~60–65%, so ARNI may be considered, especially at lower LVEF
Pre- and post-discharge initiation showed similar efficacy/safety with larger NT-proBNP reduction vs ACE-I
cautions: More frequent symptomatic hypotension
Wash-out ≥36 h after ACE-I
Same caution thresholds as ACE-I (SBP <100, eGFR <30, K⁺ >5.2); avoid abrupt withdrawal
Not recommended in pregnancy

name: Candesartan
summary: Recommended in HFrEF for patients who cannot tolerate an ACE-I or ARNI. Much lower incidence of cough and angio-oedema than ACE-I (no kininase inhibition). No ARB has reduced all-cause mortality in any trial; combining with an ACE-I increases adverse effects.
points: CHARM-Alternative: reduced CV death and HFH in ACE-I-intolerant patients
CHARM-Preserved: primary endpoint neutral; fewer HFH in LVEF 40–49% (retrospective)
cautions: Evidence limited at higher LVEF

name: Losartan
summary: Recommended in HFrEF for patients who cannot tolerate an ACE-I or ARNI. Much lower incidence of cough and angio-oedema than ACE-I (no kininase inhibition). No ARB has reduced all-cause mortality in any trial; combining with an ACE-I increases adverse effects.
points: HEAAL: high-dose losartan reduced HFH vs low dose in ACE-I-intolerant patients

name: Valsartan
summary: Recommended in HFrEF for patients who cannot tolerate an ACE-I or ARNI. Much lower incidence of cough and angio-oedema than ACE-I (no kininase inhibition). No ARB has reduced all-cause mortality in any trial; combining with an ACE-I increases adverse effects.
points: Val-HeFT: reduced HFH on top of usual therapy including ACE-I

name: Bisoprolol
summary: Reduce morbidity and mortality in HFrEF on top of ACE-I and diuretics. Start early in clinically stable patients at low dose and uptitrate gradually to the highest tolerated dose; continue long-term even if symptoms do not improve.
points: Shown to reduce risk of death in HFrEF
β1-selective: acceptable in pregnancy with HFrEF (switch from non-selective agents)
cautions: Ensure euvolaemia before initiation
In decompensated HF, initiate cautiously in hospital once haemodynamically stabilized
Effect in HFrEF with AF is uncertain (no dedicated RCT), although useful for rate control
Temporary discontinuation advised in severe haemodynamic instability

name: Carvedilol
summary: Reduce morbidity and mortality in HFrEF on top of ACE-I and diuretics. Start early in clinically stable patients at low dose and uptitrate gradually to the highest tolerated dose; continue long-term even if symptoms do not improve.
points: Shown to reduce risk of death in HFrEF
Maximum 50 mg b.i.d. may be given to patients >85 kg (Table 11, footnote d)
cautions: Ensure euvolaemia before initiation
In decompensated HF, initiate cautiously in hospital once haemodynamically stabilized
Effect in HFrEF with AF is uncertain (no dedicated RCT), although useful for rate control
Temporary discontinuation advised in severe haemodynamic instability

name: Metoprolol succinate (CR/XL)
summary: Reduce morbidity and mortality in HFrEF on top of ACE-I and diuretics. Start early in clinically stable patients at low dose and uptitrate gradually to the highest tolerated dose; continue long-term even if symptoms do not improve.
points: Sustained-release succinate shown to reduce risk of death in HFrEF
β1-selective: acceptable in pregnancy with HFrEF
cautions: Ensure euvolaemia before initiation
In decompensated HF, initiate cautiously in hospital once haemodynamically stabilized
Effect in HFrEF with AF is uncertain (no dedicated RCT), although useful for rate control
Temporary discontinuation advised in severe haemodynamic instability

name: Nebivolol
summary: Reduce morbidity and mortality in HFrEF on top of ACE-I and diuretics. Start early in clinically stable patients at low dose and uptitrate gradually to the highest tolerated dose; continue long-term even if symptoms do not improve.
points: Only reduced the combined endpoint of all-cause mortality and CV hospitalization (not shown to reduce CV/all-cause death alone)
cautions: Ensure euvolaemia before initiation
In decompensated HF, initiate cautiously in hospital once haemodynamically stabilized
Effect in HFrEF with AF is uncertain (no dedicated RCT), although useful for rate control
Temporary discontinuation advised in severe haemodynamic instability

name: Eplerenone
summary: Recommended in all symptomatic HF regardless of LVEF (steroidal MRA for HFrEF; steroidal or non-steroidal MRA for HFpEF); reduce HFH or CV death. Mortality reduction demonstrated in HFrEF only. Eplerenone and finerenone are more receptor-specific and cause less gynaecomastia.
points: Studied only in HFrEF (LVEF up to 35%)
Class I (B1) after MI with LVEF ≤40% and signs of HF or diabetes
cautions: Not tested at eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73 m²; use caution when K⁺ ≥5.0 mmol/L
If K⁺ >5.5 mEq/L: recheck, then consider dose reduction or temporary discontinuation; restart when hyperkalaemia resolves
Severe hyperkalaemia (K⁺ >5.5 or >6 mmol/L) → temporary down-titration/discontinuation of MRA and/or ACE-I/ARB/ARNI
Not recommended in pregnancy

name: Spironolactone
summary: Recommended in all symptomatic HF regardless of LVEF (steroidal MRA for HFrEF; steroidal or non-steroidal MRA for HFpEF); reduce HFH or CV death. Mortality reduction demonstrated in HFrEF only. Eplerenone and finerenone are more receptor-specific and cause less gynaecomastia.
points: Optional 12.5 mg start where kidney status or hyperkalaemia warrant caution
Studied across LVEF ranges; TOPCAT overall neutral, but meta-analysis with FINEARTS-HF positive for LVEF >40%
cautions: Not tested at eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73 m²; use caution when K⁺ ≥5.0 mmol/L
If K⁺ >5.5 mEq/L: recheck, then consider dose reduction or temporary discontinuation; restart when hyperkalaemia resolves
Severe hyperkalaemia (K⁺ >5.5 or >6 mmol/L) → temporary down-titration/discontinuation of MRA and/or ACE-I/ARB/ARNI
Not recommended in pregnancy

name: Finerenone
summary: Non-steroidal MRA studied in patients with LVEF >40% (FINEARTS-HF reduced HFH + CV death). Also recommended to reduce HF risk in T2DM with CKD (prevention).
points: Start/target dose depends on eGFR (Table 11 footnote g)
cautions: Not tested at eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73 m²; use caution when K⁺ ≥5.0 mmol/L
If K⁺ >5.5 mEq/L: recheck, then consider dose reduction or temporary discontinuation; restart when hyperkalaemia resolves
Severe hyperkalaemia (K⁺ >5.5 or >6 mmol/L) → temporary down-titration/discontinuation of MRA and/or ACE-I/ARB/ARNI
Not recommended in pregnancy
note: Dose pairing interpreted from Table 11 footnote g — verify against the PDF.

name: Dapagliflozin
summary: Recommended in all symptomatic HF regardless of LVEF to reduce HFH or CV death; also improve QoL. CV mortality reduction only in HFrEF (in HFpEF benefit driven by fewer HFH). Initiate in hospital after stabilization in decompensated HF.
cautions: Common side effects: genital and urinary tract infections
Mild initial eGFR decline expected; long-term kidney function improved

name: Empagliflozin
summary: Recommended in all symptomatic HF regardless of LVEF to reduce HFH or CV death; also improve QoL. CV mortality reduction only in HFrEF (in HFpEF benefit driven by fewer HFH). Initiate in hospital after stabilization in decompensated HF.
cautions: Common side effects: genital and urinary tract infections
Mild initial eGFR decline expected; long-term kidney function improved

name: Loop diuretics
summary: Recommended to relieve congestion in HF with volume overload; dynamic, individualized dosing guided by volume status (Class I A). Use the lowest dose that maintains euvolaemia; needs fall with optimal FMT/GDIT. Effects on morbidity/mortality not studied in adequately powered RCTs.
points: Best strategy: multiparameter assessment (clinical at rest and dynamic manoeuvres, eGFR, electrolytes, natriuretic peptides ± imaging)
In decompensated HF: IV loop diuretics for all patients with fluid overload (I A)
Add short-term IV acetazolamide or oral hydrochlorothiazide if fluid overload persists on loop diuretics (IIa B1)
Urinary Na⁺-guided diuretic therapy may be considered (IIb B1)
cautions: Electrolyte disturbances, neurohormonal activation, kidney function decline, symptomatic hypotension
Avoid chronic thiazide use in stable patients (severe, undetected electrolyte disturbances)

name: Potassium binders (patiromer, sodium zirconium cyclosilicate)
summary: Gastrointestinal K⁺ binders can treat/prevent hyperkalaemia and facilitate continuation/uptitration of ACE-I/ARNI/ARB and MRA. No specific recommendation in the guideline: clinical-outcome benefit unproven.
points: REALIZE-K: signal towards more HF deterioration with sodium zirconium cyclosilicate vs placebo (not powered for outcomes)
cautions: GI symptoms; hypomagnesaemia (patiromer); oedema (sodium zirconium cyclosilicate)

name: Ivabradine
summary: Slows heart rate via If-current inhibition. Should be considered in symptomatic HFrEF, LVEF ≤35%, sinus rhythm, resting HR above 70 b.p.m., on highest tolerated FMT (IIa B1), or if beta-blocker not tolerated (IIa C). SHIFT: benefit driven mainly by fewer HFH.
points: Initiate/uptitrate beta-blockers to target first, then reassess resting heart rate before adding ivabradine
cautions: Not recommended in pregnancy

name: Vericiguat
summary: Oral soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator; may be considered in symptomatic HFrEF with LVEF <45% despite optimal FMT (IIb B1). VICTORIA (recent worsening HF): lower CV death/HFH, no reduction in death. VICTOR (stable ambulatory, LVEF ≤40%): neutral on primary endpoint.
points: Less benefit seen at the highest NT-proBNP levels in VICTORIA

name: Hydralazine + isosorbide dinitrate
summary: Considered (IIa B2) in self-identified black patients with symptomatic HFrEF, LVEF ≤40%, on top of optimal FMT (reduced mortality and HFH, improved QoL in a small RCT). May be considered (IIb C) in HFrEF patients who cannot tolerate ACE-I, ARNI or ARB.
points: Benefit in non-black patients unclear
Older evidence (V-HeFT, male patients on digoxin + diuretics) underpins the intolerance recommendation

name: Digoxin
summary: Should be considered in symptomatic HFrEF with LVEF ≤40% despite optimal FMT to reduce HFH (IIa B1). DIG: neutral on mortality, fewer HFH. Also IIa C for AF rate control when beta-blockers are insufficient or not tolerated.
points: Target serum concentration <1.2 ng/mL
Eliminated mainly by the kidneys
cautions: Narrow therapeutic window — careful monitoring

name: Digitoxin
summary: DIGIT-HF (HFrEF, NYHA III/IV or LVEF ≤30% NYHA II): composite of all-cause death or HFH 39.5% vs 44.1% (HR 0.82); neither death nor HFH alone significant. Considered with digoxin as a cardiac glycoside (IIa B1).
points: Target serum 10.5–23.6 nmol/L in DIGIT-HF
Eliminated by hepatic metabolism
cautions: Narrow therapeutic window — careful monitoring

name: Omecamtiv mecarbil
summary: GALACTIC-HF: modest reduction in HF events without a mortality benefit. Not currently approved for clinical use in HF.

name: Intravenous iron (iron deficiency)
summary: Recommended in symptomatic HFrEF with iron deficiency to alleviate symptoms and improve QoL (I B1); should be considered to reduce HFH (IIa B1).
points: Iron status (TSAT, ferritin) is part of the initial laboratory work-up

name: Semaglutide / tirzepatide
summary: Should be considered in symptomatic HF with LVEF ≥45% and BMI ≥30 kg/m², regardless of diabetes status, to reduce weight and improve exercise capacity and QoL (IIa B1). Prevention: GLP-1 RA in T2DM with another CV risk factor (IIa A).

name: Oral anticoagulants (DOACs, VKAs)
summary: Oral anticoagulation is recommended in HF with clinical AF at elevated thromboembolic risk by CHA₂DS₂-VA (I A); DOACs preferred over VKAs (I B1). Patients with HCM and cardiac amyloidosis need anticoagulation irrespective of score.

name: AF rate/rhythm drugs (beta-blockers, digoxin, amiodarone)
summary: HFrEF with AF: beta-blockers first-line for rate control (I C); digoxin if rate remains high or beta-blockers not tolerated (IIa C); IV amiodarone or digoxin for acute rate control in haemodynamically unstable patients (IIb C). Urgent cardioversion if rapid rates with haemodynamic instability (I C).

name: Acute decompensated HF agents (oxygen, vasodilators, inotropes, vasopressors, opiates)
summary: Oxygen if SpO₂ <90% or PaO₂ <60 mmHg (I C). IV vasodilators may be considered if SBP >110 mmHg (IIb C). Inotropes may be considered if SBP <90 mmHg with hypoperfusion unresponsive to standard treatment (IIb C). Vasopressors, preferably norepinephrine, in cardiogenic shock (IIb C). Routine opiates not recommended (III C).

name: TTR-directed therapy (vutrisiran, tafamidis, acoramidis)
summary: TTR silencer (vutrisiran) or stabilizer (tafamidis or acoramidis) is recommended in variant or wild-type ATTR cardiac amyloidosis, NYHA I–III, to reduce symptom progression, CV hospitalization and death (I A).

name: Drugs to avoid or use with caution (NSAIDs/COX-2, pregnancy)
summary: NSAIDs and COX-2 inhibitors are not recommended (III B2) — they worsen HF and increase HFH. In pregnancy, ACE-I, ARB, ARNI, MRA, ivabradine and SGLT2-I are not recommended (foetotoxicity/teratogenicity); non-selective beta-blockers should be switched to β1-selective agents (metoprolol, bisoprolol). Glucose-lowering drugs without proven HF safety should be avoided in prevention.
